note: These period names come mainly from European history-writing and overlap in time. Other regions use their own periods (for example Japan's Heian or Edo periods), which appear in each country's history.

periods.label: Prehistory
periods.blurb: Farming began independently in several regions after the last Ice Age, and the first villages and towns appeared.

periods.label: Ancient civilisations
periods.blurb: Writing, cities and kingdoms emerged along great rivers — the Nile, Tigris and Euphrates, Indus and Yellow River.

periods.label: Classical antiquity
periods.blurb: The age of Greece, Rome, Persia, the Maurya and Gupta empires of India, and Han China.

periods.label: Middle Ages
periods.blurb: Islamic caliphates, the Byzantine Empire, Tang and Song China, the Mongol Empire, and Southeast Asia's maritime powers such as Srivijaya.

periods.label: Renaissance
periods.blurb: A revival of classical learning and art that began in Italian city-states and spread across Europe.

periods.label: Age of Exploration
periods.blurb: European ships reached the Americas and sailed around Africa into the Indian Ocean; Melaka fell to Portugal in 1511.

periods.label: Colonial era
periods.blurb: European powers built empires across the Americas, Africa and Asia; most colonies won independence after 1945.

periods.label: Industrial Revolution
periods.blurb: Steam power, factories and railways transformed Britain, then Europe, North America and Japan.

periods.label: World War I
periods.blurb: A global war centred on Europe that ended four empires: the German, Austro-Hungarian, Russian and Ottoman.

periods.label: World War II
periods.blurb: The deadliest conflict in history, fought across Europe, Africa, Asia and the Pacific.

periods.label: Cold War
periods.blurb: Rivalry between the United States and the Soviet Union, and the era when most of Asia and Africa became independent.

periods.label: Contemporary
periods.blurb: The world since the end of the Cold War: globalisation, the internet and new regional powers.
